newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin sees 1998 GDP growth of 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin sees 1998 GDP growth of 6.0 pct.

text.p: Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Tuesday he expects the Thai economy to expand by at least six percent in 1998 after slowing down below projected targets this year following the baht flotation.

"After the change in the baht value and higher inflation this year, the GDP (gross domestic product) growth should be lower than the government-projected 5.7 percent growth but by how much still remains to be seen," Thanong said.
"I believe that economic growth in 1998 would be six percent or more," he told a seminar.

Last week financial authorities changed the currency to a managed float from a 13-year old system of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies. After the float the baht dropped in value by about 20 percent in offshore markets.
